2. The facts, in short, are that the respondent as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 138 of 1994 against the defendant appellant for declaration that letter addressed to the plaintiff respondent by the defendant under Memo No. A (421) DA/93/51 dated 23.3.1994 for cancellation of allotment of house No. 5/4, Block-E, Lalmatia to the plaintiff respondent vide letter dated 1.8.1972 is void and illegal. The plaintiff respondent was an Assistant Professor of medicine in the P.G. Hospital and he had served in different positions and departments till he retired from service on 3.12.1993. While he was in service he resided in the house in question, an abandoned house, allotted to him by the Government to reside there on payment of standard rent. On 3.11.1993 one month before his retirement the plaintiff respondent informed the Government that he was going to retire on 3.12.1993 and asked for fixing of rent of the said house. Instead of fixing rent the Government by the impugned letter cancelled the plaintiff's allotment under Rule 15(2)(3) of the Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982. 

 3. The plaintiff filed an application for temporary injunction with prayer for ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants from evicting the plaintiff from the suit premises which was summarily rejected by the trial court on the finding that in the letter dated 1.8.1972 by which the suit house was allotted to the plaintiff by the Ministry of Works it is stated that the said plaintiff allotted will have to vacate the premises when requited by the Government. 

 4. An appeal was preferred by the plaintiff, being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 119 of 1994, and the appellate court by judgment and order dated 31.7.1991 dismissed the appeal and upheld the judgment and order passed by the trial court. 

 5. The plaintiff respondent then moved the high Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2756 of 1994 and a rule was obtained which was subsequently made absolute on the ground:- 

 "The cause of the dispute is that whether the plaintiff is an allotted of the house as a residential quarter as a government servant or he is a permanent lessee of the house, in question an abandoned property and whether the allotment shall be treated as an allotment of a quarter for residential purpose of the plaintiff as a government servant and whether the notice for eviction is a valid one. These things shall be decided in the suit when it is disposed of finally of evidences." 

 6. " If the plaintiff is evicted during the pendency of the suit from his residential house refusing to grant injunction in my view, it will be pre-empting the whole dispute and it will be a pre-mature decision upon the merits of the suit itself and if ultimately the plaintiffs wins the suit, he will incur irreparable loss. So the prima facie case and the balance of convenience stet inconvenience is in favour of the plaintiff. Therefore by refusing to grant temporary injunction during the pendency of the suit in my view the courts below have committed illegality resulting on error in the decisions occasioning failure of Justice..:" 

 8. Mr. Farid Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the appellant I submits that the plaintiff was an Assistant Professor of P.G. Hospital and the abandoned house was allotted to him on temporary basis for residential purpose and he is bound to vacate the same after expiry of 6(six) months from his admitted retirement on 4.12.1993 in terms of Rule 15(2)(3) of the Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982. 

 9. He further submits that the plaintiff himself   by invoicing Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982 applied for extension for a further period of one year after his retirement on the ground of education of his youngest son. Therefore, he cannot take belated plea that the Allocation Rules, 1982 does not apply. 

 10. Lastly, the High Court Division has failed to consider that the plaintiff has no subsisting right to continue to occupy the suit house. Further, in view of the decisions passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 66 of 1986 and Civil Appeal No. 1158 of 1997 the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is apparently erroneous and not sustainable. 

 12. We have considered the submissions of the teamed Deputy Attorney General and the papers annexed to the appeal. Annexure-A, the allotemnt letter specifically contains a term to the following effect, "The allottee would vacate the premises whenever required by the Government." Therefore, the allotment of the aforesaid house was given on a temporary basis with a discretion given to the government to cancel it whenever it is required by the government. Moreover, a scrutiny of annexure-X, a letter to the appellant, by which the plaintiff respondent prayed for an extension of his allotment by one more year, will show that he has accepted the fact that he is a temporary allottee of the abandoned house. Annexure-A(1) will show that the Government has granted him per-mission to stay in the house for a further period of 6(six) months in accordance with Rule 15(2) (3) of the Bangladesh Allocation Rules, 1982.
